section_summary.extract_value: The section reports that young Black women in the sample selected smaller personal ideal body figures than the ethnic group ideal and that participants perceived their own bodies as smaller than typical ethnic peers despite over 40% being in the overweight/obese BMI range. The authors discuss possible influences (media, stigma, social comparison, self-discrepancy) and note this may reflect a transitional period for some Black females; no explicit study labels (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets are mentioned in the text.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The young women in our sample on average selected a smaller (low-range normal weight) figure to represent their personal ideal body size..." and "Our analyses also indicated that the figure selected to reflect participants' actual body size was on average significantly smaller than the figure selected to reflect a typical ethnic female peer despite more than 40% of the sample possessing a BMI in the overweight or obese range."
